title: TTK Prestige Ltd - 517506 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: TTK Prestige Q2 FY27: revenue up about 21.9% with domestic up 23.4% and operating EBITDA up about 70.9%, but cost inflation is set to pressure gross margin.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a strong quarter, with top-line growth backed by consumer demand, premiumization, and new product launches. Domestic sales grew about 23.4% and operating EBITDA about 70.9%, per management's remarks on the call. Input cost inflation across roughly 95% of input line items is the main concern, and management said price increases have been staggered and only partly absorbed. Two exceptional items were booked this quarter: the exit from the 51% subsidiary Ultra Fresh Modular Solution and a loss of about Rs 2 crore on a compulsory convertible debenture in a rural distribution startup that shut down.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 18 crore in Q2 FY26 strategic expenses, which did not recur

financial_highlights.value: Ultra Fresh investment exit (amount not stated) and Rs 2 crore CCD write-off

segments.name: Cookers
segments.commentary: Around 30-32% of revenue per management's breakdown in the investor presentation.

segments.name: Cookware
segments.commentary: Around 15-18% of revenue. Tri-ply is growing about 1.5 times the industry average, and enamel cookware is an early new launch.

segments.name: Appliances
segments.commentary: Close to 50% of revenue. Appliances are outsourced to exclusive partners. Induction is growing faster than the company, with management guiding to high-teens growth for the category.

guidance_outlook: Cost inflation is expected to keep flowing through the next few quarters, with more price increases needed; management said recovery through price is difficult and gross margin pressure will start to show.
Soft expense plan is Rs 200-250 crore over three years, with about Rs 100 crore spent over the last six to eight quarters and about Rs 150 crore still to be spent over the remaining year.
Management reiterated a 13-14% EBITDA margin band but said it will be cautious given cost volatility.
Some festive-season sales are expected to flow into Q3 FY27.
Industry growth outlook is high-teens for the category, with management calling growth sustainable though less dramatic than recent quarters.
capex_capacity: Ultra Fresh Modular Solution (51% subsidiary) investment exited; management said the focus is the core categories and markets.
Strategic spend is shifting from capability building toward brand and innovation in the next few quarters.
Ninety percent of kitchenware is manufactured in-house; appliances are outsourced to exclusive partners.
Tri-ply cookware inputs are partly sourced from China (no domestic source cited).
demand_pricing: Industry demand is recovering after a lull, supported by urban premiumization, kitchen modernization, and migration from unorganized to organized players due to cost pressure.
Price increases were taken in a step jump but staggered; management said the industry has not fully absorbed the cost increase.
Commodity inputs (aluminium, stainless steel, rubber, chemicals, packaging) are up, with current prices above Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 levels, and old-cost inventory is now used up.
E-commerce plus quick commerce is about 20% of sales; growth is described as even across channels.
Competition is mainly from digital-first brands in cookware, and management has not yet seen their impact on growth.
Judge brand is positioned lower in the mass market, with a structurally lower margin than Prestige; management declined to quantify the gap.

qa_highlights.question: Which commodities are driving cost increases, and are competitors taking price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 95% of input line items are affected, including packaging, handles, rubber and chemicals. Price increases were taken in a staggered manner and the industry has not fully absorbed the costs.

qa_highlights.question: How much soft expense has been spent and how much is budgeted?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 85-100 crore was spent last year and Rs 13 crore in H1 FY27. The plan is Rs 200-250 crore over three years, and spend is being realigned toward brand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory build and why did cash flow come under pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the build reflects demand anticipation and manufacturing changes, and that inventory days have not risen; the absolute value is higher because of the growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost pressure in RM and will pricing continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Costs are still above Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 levels. Management said old-cost inventory benefits are used up, so pressure will reach gross margin, and more price action is possible.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Judge brand cannibalizing Prestige, and what is its margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cannibalization is minimal because the brands target different segments. Judge is positioned at the lower end of the mass market with a slightly lower margin than Prestige, but no figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall YoY and QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 FY26 included about Rs 18 crore of strategic expenses that did not recur, and cost optimization benefits are flowing through. More strategic spend is planned.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from RM inflation, with management saying price increases may not fully offset costs.
Demand elasticity if price increases continue, which management flagged as a concern.
Competition from digital-first cookware brands, whose impact is not yet visible.
Soft expense spend of about Rs 150 crore still to come, which could weigh on EBITDA.
Inventory build straining cash flow, with the absolute level higher despite stable inventory days.
Export business under pressure from geopolitical and UK/Europe macro conditions.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, premiumization, and market share gains, but cautious on input cost inflation and its impact on margins. Management was evasive on specific numbers, declining to give channel-wise growth, Judge margin figures, the enamel market size, and the pricing ask.
key_quotes: We have been delivering higher market shares with profitable growth and that would be the way forward as we speak driven by premiumization, innovation and a lot more focus on new product development and deliverable to the market as well.
the cost increases are at a stage where it probably would affect demand and therefore I think we would want to look at it more from a perspective of a stable environment over a period of time.
Even today the price is much higher than what it used to be in the Q4 of last year or the Q1 of this year.
Judge would have a slightly lower margin profile.

growth.why: Q2 revenue up about 21.9% (domestic +23.4%) on volume (8-9 pts), premiumization and launches, but management guided only to a 13-14% EBITDA margin band with caution and warned gross margin pressure will show; no capacity additions or order book cited, so backing is vague.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management flagged gross margin pressure from RM inflation (about 95% of input line items affected) with old-cost inventory now used up, and reiterated a 13-14% EBITDA margin band only with caution.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 FY27 volume contributed about 8-9 points of the 22% sales growth, industry demand is recovering, and some festive sales are expected to flow into Q3 FY27, though management said growth will be less dramatic than recent quarters.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure was given and 90% of kitchenware is already made in-house; the capex read is not discussed, and the Ultra Fresh investment was exited rather than expanded.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management kept the 13-14% EBITDA margin band but said it will be cautious given cost volatility, with more price increases needed and no raised guidance cited.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gross margin pressure will show as cost inflation flows through, and about Rs 150 crore of soft spend remains to be spent over the next year against a 13-14% EBITDA band.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Enamel cookware is an early new launch, tri-ply is growing about 1.5 times the industry average, and management is shifting strategic spend toward brand and innovation over the next few quarters.

rows.label: Further price increases to offset RM inflation
rows.why: Costs remain above Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 levels and management said more price action is possible, but also said recovery through price is difficult and demand elasticity is a concern.

rows.label: Lapping of Rs 18 crore non-recurring strategic spend
rows.why: Q2 FY26 included about Rs 18 crore of strategic expenses that did not recur, which supports the YoY other-expense comparison, though about Rs 150 crore of soft spend is still to come.

rows.label: Inventory build straining cash flow
rows.why: Absolute inventory is higher with growth and cash flow came under pressure, though management said inventory days have not risen.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, premiumization and share gains but cautious on input cost inflation and margins; analysts pressed on pricing, soft expense and inventory, and management was evasive on Judge margins, channel growth and the pricing ask.
